builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: HRTF Upsampling and Personalization via Neural Operators
summary: SPARO replaces per-subject neural-field fitting and classical spherical-harmonic interpolation for HRTF upsampling with a single learned operator that encodes sparse measurements into spherical latent modes, processes them with Transformer blocks, and decodes at arbitrary query directions. The cost is training a domain-specific model on HRTF datasets such as SONICOM or HUTUBS plus the measurement apparatus needed to obtain the sparse per-subject samples, neither of which is an LLM-inference concern. It can fail on subjects or measurement geometries outside the training distribution, and its ITD error is only competitive rather than best, which matters for localization accuracy.
rationale: This is a specialized binaural-audio signal processing method with no bearing on LLM training, inference, or agent systems, so it only matters if the reader's production work is personalized spatial audio.
technique: Neural operator for HRTF spatial upsampling

claims.statement: SPARO replaces per-subject neural-field fitting and classical spherical-harmonic interpolation for HRTF upsampling with a single learned operator that encodes sparse measurements into spherical latent modes, processes them with Transformer blocks, and decodes at arbitrary query directions. The cost is training a domain-specific model on HRTF datasets such as SONICOM or HUTUBS plus the measurement apparatus needed to obtain the sparse per-subject samples, neither of which is an LLM-inference concern. It can fail on subjects or measurement geometries outside the training distribution, and its ITD error is only competitive rather than best, which matters for localization accuracy.
15 to 373 times faster dense HRTF reconstruction than the RANF neural-field baseline, with 18% lower log-spectral distortion and 43% lower ILD error at 100 measurements on SONICOM.
